page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by first-generation AMD EPYC 7571 processors. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Complementing the core compute resources is 2,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark telemetry highlights a distinct separation between single-threaded throughput and parallelized operations. The underlying Zen microarchitecture delivers modest single-core execution speed, ranking in the lower 10% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain within the middle 50% tier, showing steady scaling across all 64 vCPUs for parallel processing, compilation tasks, and decompression. Memory subsystem performance is stable, delivering 107.11 GB/s of uncached sequential read bandwidth and 52.78 GB/s write bandwidth. The integrated hardware cryptographic extensions drive strong cryptographic benchmark scores, placing the instance in the top 25%.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the r5ad.16xlarge provides high memory and local storage density for workloads where peak single-core clock frequency is not a requirement. Bundling 2.4 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage eliminates external block storage overhead for scratch volumes and high-speed temporary caching. This configuration fits distributed in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, relational databases, data warehousing staging layers, and distributed memory-resident data analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The platform is provisioned with 512 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 2,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a 12 Gbps baseline network link. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits modest single-thread execution metrics, falling into lower performance tiers, but balances this with reliable mid-tier multi-threaded throughput and strong hardware-accelerated cryptographic processing. Its local NVMe storage combined with high memory capacity provides an efficient platform for memory-intensive applications requiring local temporary persistence. The r5ad.16xlarge is suited for in-memory key-value databases like Redis, medium-scale data warehousing staging, relational database hosting, and distributed memory-heavy data analytics where per-thread compute latency is secondary to aggregate memory volume.
